lessons.title: Χαιρετισμοί & Γνωριμία (Greetings & Introductions)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Formal & informal greetings, polite addresses, personal pronouns, and core verbs (είμαι, λέω, γράφω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 1 Core Grammar Notes:
• Vocative Singular: Masculine nouns in -ος end in -ε (κύριε Παπαδόπουλε). Feminine nouns in -α/-η remain unchanged (κυρία, δεσποινίς).
• Copular Verb 'είμαι' (Present): εγώ είμαι, εσύ είσαι, αυτός/αυτή/αυτό είναι, εμείς είμαστε, εσείς είστε, αυτοί/αυτές/αυτά είναι.
• Stating Names: 'Με λένε + Accusative' (e.g. Με λένε Κώστα) or 'Είμαι ο/η + Nominative'.

entries.notes: Vocative singular drops final -ς and changes to -ε (κύριε).
entries.example_el: Γεια σας, κύριε Παπαδόπουλε.
entries.example_en: Hello, Mr. Papadopoulos.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Addressing individuals politely and formal introductions

entries.notes: Vocative singular is identical to nominative: κυρία.
entries.example_el: Αυτή είναι η κυρία Καραγιάννη.
entries.example_en: This is Mrs. Karagianni.

entries.notes: In daily spoken Greek, often truncated to the vocative particle 'δεσποινίς'.
entries.example_el: Καλημέρα σας, δεσποινίς Ελένη.
entries.example_en: Good morning, Miss Eleni.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite address to an unmarried young woman

entries.notes: Neuter noun in -μα; plural adds -τα (τα ονόματα). Takes a second accent before possessive clitic: το όνομά μου.
entries.example_el: Ποιο είναι το όνομά σου;
entries.example_en: What is your name?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for and stating names in introductions

entries.notes: Proparoxytone noun (accent on antepenult). Takes an enclitic accent before possessive: το επώνυμό μου.
entries.example_el: Το επώνυμό μου είναι Αντωνίου.
entries.example_en: My last name is Antoniou.

entries.notes: Neuter noun in -μα (plural: τα γράμματα). Essential for KEG listening task on name spelling.
entries.example_el: Ποιο είναι το πρώτο γράμμα;
entries.example_en: What is the first letter?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Spelling Greek names and asking about the alphabet

entries.notes: Vocative singular: (ε) φίλε μου! Note masculine nominative article 'ο'.
entries.example_el: Αυτός είναι ο φίλος μου, ο Νίκος.
entries.example_en: This is my friend, Nikos.

entries.notes: Regular feminine in -η with plural in -ες. Accusative drops final -ν before fricatives (τη φίλη).
entries.example_el: Αυτή είναι η φίλη μου, η Μαρία.
entries.example_en: This is my friend, Maria.

entries.notes: Copular auxiliary verb. Full present paradigm: είμαι, είσαι, είναι, είμαστε, είστε (είσαστε), είναι.
entries.example_el: Εγώ είμαι ο Γιώργος.
entries.example_en: I am Giorgos.

entries.english: to say / to tell / to call
entries.notes: 'Με λένε + Accusative' literally means 'They call me'. Most natural everyday way to state your name.
entries.example_el: Με λένε Κώστα και είμαι μαθητής.
entries.example_en: My name is Kostas and I am a student.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating one's name via direct object formula ('με λένε')

entries.notes: Model Type A regular active verb (-ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν).
entries.example_el: Πώς γράφετε το όνομά σας;
entries.example_en: How do you write (spell) your name?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking how names and contact information are spelled

entries.notes: Modern Greek is a pro-drop language; 'εγώ' is reserved for emphasis or contrast.
entries.example_el: Εγώ είμαι από την Ελλάδα, εσύ;
entries.example_en: I am from Greece, and you?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Emphasizing personal identity or contrasting with others

entries.notes: Informal address. Contrasts strictly with the formal polite 'εσείς'.
entries.example_el: Εσύ πώς είσαι σήμερα;
entries.example_en: How are you today?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Directly addressing a friend, colleague, or child

entries.notes: Functions both as 3rd person subject pronoun ('he') and demonstrative ('this').
entries.example_el: Αυτός είναι ο δάσκαλός μας.
entries.example_en: He is our teacher.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing and pointing out a male individual

entries.notes: Feminine nominative singular. Plural is 'αυτές'.
entries.example_el: Αυτή είναι η Άννα.
entries.example_en: She is Anna.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Introducing and pointing out a female individual

entries.notes: Neuter singular. Universal question prompt in KEG A1 listening items: 'Τι είναι αυτό;'.
entries.example_el: Τι είναι αυτό;
entries.example_en: What is this?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about or identifying objects and concepts

entries.notes: Triggers 1st person plural verb ending -ουμε / -μαστε.
entries.example_el: Εμείς είμαστε μαθητές.
entries.example_en: We are students.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing shared identity or group actions

entries.notes: The plural of courtesy (πληθυντικός ευγενείας). Essential KEG A1 social competence marker.
entries.example_el: Εσείς από πού είστε;
entries.example_en: Where are you from? (formal or plural)
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite formula for addressing adult strangers or a group

entries.notes: Gender agreement is mandatory in 3rd person plural: άντρες -> αυτοί, γυναίκες -> αυτές, πράγματα -> αυτά.
entries.example_el: Αυτοί είναι οι νέοι συμμαθητές μας.
entries.example_en: They are our new classmates.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying multiple third persons or objects

entries.notes: Always takes a written accent (τόνος) in questions to distinguish from the conjunction 'πως' (that).
entries.example_el: Πώς σε λένε;
entries.example_en: What is your name? (Literally: How do they call you?)
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about well-being, names, and methods

entries.notes: Always accented. Agrees in gender with the referenced noun: ποιος είναι αυτός; / ποια είναι αυτή;.
entries.example_el: Ποιος είναι αυτός ο κύριος;
entries.example_en: Who is that gentleman?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about the identity of specific persons or objects

entries.notes: Monosyllabic and never accented. 'Τι κάνεις;' is the ubiquitous everyday Greek greeting.
entries.example_el: Τι κάνεις;
entries.example_en: How are you doing? / What are you doing?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for information about things, actions, and states

entries.notes: Derived from 'υγεία σου' (to your health). Used symmetrically for both 'hello' and 'goodbye'.
entries.example_el: Γεια σου, Ελένη! Τι νέα;
entries.example_en: Hi, Eleni! What's new?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting or saying farewell to friends, family, and peers

entries.notes: Standard formal opening for KEG oral examination interviews.
entries.example_el: Γεια σας, κύριε καθηγητά.
entries.example_en: Hello, professor.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting professionals, elders, strangers, or multiple people

entries.notes: Compound of καλή + μέρα. Written as a single word with accent on -ε-.
entries.example_el: Καλημέρα σε όλους!
entries.example_en: Good morning to everyone!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Standard daytime greeting from dawn until early afternoon

entries.notes: Used exclusively as a greeting upon arrival/meeting, never as a farewell.
entries.example_el: Καλησπέρα σας, τι κάνετε;
entries.example_en: Good evening, how are you?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Greeting upon arrival from mid-afternoon onward

entries.notes: Strictly a parting farewell before sleep; never used as a greeting upon arrival.
entries.example_el: Καληνύχτα και καλό ξημέρωμα!
entries.example_en: Good night and sleep well!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Wishing someone a good night when taking leave or sleeping

entries.notes: Often paired with 'σας' in polite social contexts: Αντίο σας.
entries.example_el: Αντίο σας, καλό απόγευμα.
entries.example_en: Goodbye, have a pleasant afternoon.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Formal or standard farewell when departing

entries.notes: Literally: 'We say them'. The most frequent casual goodbye in modern Greece.
entries.example_el: Τα λέμε αύριο στο μάθημα!
entries.example_en: See you tomorrow in class!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Informal parting formula between friends and colleagues

entries.notes: Diphthong 'ευ' is pronounced as /ef/ before voiceless 'χ'. Often emphasized as 'ευχαριστώ πολύ'.
entries.example_el: Ευχαριστώ πολύ για τη βοήθεια.
entries.example_en: Thank you very much for the help.

entries.notes: Two-way usage: 'please' when ordering/asking, and 'you are welcome' after 'ευχαριστώ'.
entries.example_el: Έναν καφέ, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A coffee, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Polite requests and responding to thanks

entries.notes: Spelled with double γ (γγ pronounced as velar nasal [ŋ]).
entries.example_el: Συγγνώμη, ποιος είναι ο καθηγητής;
entries.example_en: Excuse me, who is the professor?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Apologizing or politely getting someone's attention

entries.english: pleased to meet you / nice to meet you
entries.notes: Standard social formula taught formulaically at A1 upon hearing someone's name.
entries.example_el: — Είμαι ο Γιάννης. — Χάρηκα, είμαι η Σοφία.
entries.example_en: — I am Giannis. — Pleased to meet you, I am Sofia.

entries.notes: Adverbial form (πολύ). Must not be confused with the inflected adjective 'πολύς'.
entries.example_el: Είμαι πολύ καλά, ευχαριστώ.
entries.example_en: I am very well, thank you.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Modifying adjectives, adverbs, and verbs to express high degree

entries.notes: Adverb formed from the neuter plural of the adjective 'καλός'.
entries.example_el: — Πώς είσαι; — Καλά, εσύ;
entries.example_en: — How are you? — Fine, and you?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating positive personal condition in greeting exchanges

lessons.title: Καταγωγή, Εθνικότητες & Γλώσσες (Origins, Nationalities & Languages)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Countries, nationalities, spoken languages, and verbs of residence & communication (μένω, μιλάω, μαθαίνω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 2 Core Grammar Notes:
• Expressing Origin: 'από + Accusative' (e.g., Από πού είσαι; — Είμαι από την Ελλάδα).
• Expressing Residence: 'σε + Accusative' contracts with article: σε + την = στην, σε + το = στο, σε + τον = στον (e.g., Μένω στην Αθήνα).
• Nationalities: Masculine in -ος/-ας/-ης, Feminine in -ίδα/-α (ο Έλληνας / η Ελληνίδα, ο Άγγλος / η Αγγλίδα).
• Languages: Neuter plural with definite article (τα ελληνικά, τα αγγλικά, τα γαλλικά).

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -α with plural in -ες. Note: 'η Χώρα' on Greek islands also refers to the main town.
entries.example_el: Από ποια χώρα είσαι;
entries.example_en: Which country are you from?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for and stating geographic origins

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -η ending in -εις in nominative plural (οι πόλεις).
entries.example_el: Η Αθήνα είναι μία μεγάλη πόλη.
entries.example_en: Athens is a big city.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating one's city of residence or origin

entries.notes: Ancient-declension neuter in -ος with plural in -η (τα κράτη).
entries.example_el: Η Ελλάδα είναι κράτος της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης.
entries.example_en: Greece is a member state of the European Union.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to geopolitical states in official contexts

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -ότητα (plural in -ότητες). Essential keyword in KEG reading forms.
entries.example_el: Ποια είναι η εθνικότητά σας;
entries.example_en: What is your nationality?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Completing official registration cards and forms

entries.notes: Commonly paired with 'έχω' + adjective of nationality in the feminine.
entries.example_el: Έχω ελληνική καταγωγή αλλά μένω στον Καναδά.
entries.example_en: I have Greek heritage but I live in Canada.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Discussing ancestral background and cultural roots

entries.notes: Regular feminine in -α with plural in -ες. Root of English 'linguistics/glossary'.
entries.example_el: Ποιες γλώσσες μιλάτε;
entries.example_en: Which languages do you speak?

entries.notes: Adjective 'μητρικός' (maternal) agrees with 'γλώσσα' in feminine nominative.
entries.example_el: Η μητρική μου γλώσσα είναι τα αγγλικά.
entries.example_en: My mother tongue is English.

entries.notes: Takes final -ν in the accusative article before vowels: 'στην Ελλάδα', 'από την Ελλάδα'.
entries.example_el: Μένω στην Ελλάδα τώρα.
entries.example_en: I live in Greece now.

entries.notes: Feminine proper noun. Accusative: την Αγγλία (keeps -ν before vowel).
entries.example_el: Ο φίλος μου είναι από την Αγγλία.
entries.example_en: My friend is from England.

entries.notes: Crucial grammatical trap: feminine gender despite ending in -ος (accusative: την Κύπρο).
entries.example_el: Η Κύπρος είναι ένα όμορφο νησί.
entries.example_en: Cyprus is a beautiful island.

entries.notes: Accusative drops -ν before γ: 'από τη Γαλλία', 'στη Γαλλία'.
entries.example_el: Η καθηγήτρια είναι από τη Γαλλία.
entries.example_en: The teacher is from France.

entries.notes: Accusative drops -ν before γ: 'στη Γερμανία'.
entries.example_el: Μένουμε στη Γερμανία.
entries.example_en: We live in Germany.

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'στην Ιταλία'.
entries.example_el: Ταξιδεύω συχνά στην Ιταλία.
entries.example_en: I travel often to Italy.

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'από την Ισπανία'.
entries.example_el: Η Μαρία είναι από την Ισπανία.
entries.example_en: Maria is from Spain.

entries.notes: Plural agreement: 'από τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες', 'στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες'.
entries.example_el: Είμαι από τις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες της Αμερικής.
entries.example_en: I am from the United States of America.

entries.notes: Accusative retains -ν before vowel: 'στην Αυστραλία'.
entries.example_el: Έχω συγγενείς στην Αυστραλία.
entries.example_en: I have relatives in Australia.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying country of origin and Greek diaspora center

entries.notes: Masculine noun in -ας; nominative plural is 'οι Έλληνες'.
entries.example_el: Ο Νίκος είναι Έλληνας.
entries.example_en: Nikos is a Greek man.

entries.notes: Feminine nationality suffix -ίδα with plural in -ίδες.
entries.example_el: Η Ελένη είναι Ελληνίδα.
entries.example_en: Eleni is a Greek woman.

entries.notes: Capitalized when denoting the national noun.
entries.example_el: Ο Τζον είναι Άγγλος.
entries.example_en: John is an Englishman.

entries.notes: Feminine nationality noun in -ίδα.
entries.example_el: Η Σάρα είναι Αγγλίδα.
entries.example_en: Sarah is an Englishwoman.

entries.notes: Regular masculine in -ος (plural: οι Γάλλοι).
entries.example_el: Ο Πιερ είναι Γάλλος φοιτητής.
entries.example_en: Pierre is a French student.

entries.notes: Feminine nationality form in -ίδα.
entries.example_el: Η Μαρί είναι Γαλλίδα.
entries.example_en: Marie is a Frenchwoman.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine (accent on final syllable -ός).
entries.example_el: Ο Χανς είναι Γερμανός.
entries.example_en: Hans is a German man.

entries.notes: Feminine nationality form in -ίδα.
entries.example_el: Η Ίνγκριντ είναι Γερμανίδα.
entries.example_en: Ingrid is a German woman.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine noun in -ός.
entries.example_el: Ο Μάρκο είναι Ιταλός.
entries.example_en: Marco is an Italian man.

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο Ιταλός.
entries.example_el: Η Τζούλια είναι Ιταλίδα.
entries.example_en: Giulia is an Italian woman.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine noun in -ός.
entries.example_el: Ο Κάρλος είναι Ισπανός.
entries.example_en: Carlos is a Spanish man.

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο Ισπανός.
entries.example_el: Η Κάρμεν είναι Ισπανίδα.
entries.example_en: Carmen is a Spanish woman.

entries.notes: Adjectives in Greek are written in lower case (ελληνικός) unlike the proper national nouns (ο Έλληνας).
entries.example_el: Μου αρέσει ο ελληνικός καφές.
entries.example_en: I like Greek coffee.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing objects, concepts, and traditions related to Greece

entries.notes: Language names in Modern Greek are grammatically neuter plural adjectives (τα ελληνικά).
entries.example_el: Μαθαίνω ελληνικά στο πανεπιστήμιο.
entries.example_en: I am learning Greek at the university.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to the Greek language as a field of study or speech

entries.notes: Neuter plural without capital letter when denoting language.
entries.example_el: Μιλάω πολύ καλά αγγλικά.
entries.example_en: I speak English very well.

entries.notes: Neuter plural language designation.
entries.example_el: Καταλαβαίνω λίγα γαλλικά.
entries.example_en: I understand a little French.

entries.english: to live / to reside / to stay
entries.notes: Type A active verb. Governs 'σε + Accusative' for location (μένω στο Παρίσι, μένω στη Ρώμη).
entries.example_el: Μένω στην Αθήνα, στην οδό Πανεπιστημίου.
entries.example_en: I live in Athens, on Panepistimiou Street.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating address, neighborhood, city, or country of residence

entries.notes: Archetypal Type B1 contracted active verb (-άω/-ώ, -άς, -άει/-ά, -άμε, -άτε, -άνε/-ούν).
entries.example_el: Μιλάω ελληνικά και αγγλικά.
entries.example_en: I speak Greek and English.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing language skills and conversational communication

entries.notes: Type A active verb with stem ending in -αιν- (-αίνω, -αίνεις, -αίνει).
entries.example_el: Μαθαίνουμε νέα ελληνικά στο σχολείο.
entries.example_en: We are learning Modern Greek at school.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about learning languages and subjects

entries.notes: Crucial survival phrase for KEG oral examination. Conjugates like μαθαίνω.
entries.example_el: Δεν καταλαβαίνω, παρακαλώ μιλάτε πιο αργά.
entries.example_en: I do not understand, please speak more slowly.

entries.notes: Type A active verb. Frequently used in questions with polite 'εσείς' (ξέρετε).
entries.example_el: Ξέρετε πού είναι το σχολείο;
entries.example_en: Do you know where the school is?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating knowledge of facts, information, or languages

entries.notes: Always governs the Accusative case: από + τον/την/το/τους/τις/τα.
entries.example_el: Είμαι από την Κύπρο.
entries.example_en: I am from Cyprus.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing origin, provenance, and nationality background

entries.notes: Contracted systematically with the definite article (στο, στη, στον, στα, στις, στους).
entries.example_el: Ζω στην Αθήνα και δουλεύω στο κέντρο.
entries.example_en: I live in Athens and work in the centre.

grammatical_info.contractions: σε + τον = στον, σε + την = στη(ν), σε + το = στο, σε + τους = στους, σε + τις = στις, σε + τα = στα

entries.notes: Adverbial modifier. Often contrasted with 'πολύ' (very / a lot).
entries.example_el: Μιλάω μόνο λίγο ελληνικά.
entries.example_en: I speak only a little Greek.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing basic or emerging language competency

units.title: Επαγγέλματα, Σπουδές & Στοιχεία Επικοινωνίας (Professions & Contact Details)

lessons.title: Επαγγέλματα, Σπουδές & Στοιχεία Επικοινωνίας (Professions & Contact Details)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Occupations, workplaces, phone numbers, addresses, digits 0-10, and verbs (δουλεύω, σπουδάζω, διδάσκω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 3 Core Grammar Notes:
• Professions & Gender Suffixes: Masculine in -ος, Feminine in -α/-ος (ο δάσκαλος / η δασκάλα, ο/η γιατρός, ο/η δικηγόρος). Masculine in -ης, Feminine in -τρια (ο καθηγητής / η καθηγήτρια, ο φοιτητής / η φοιτήτρια).
• Asking about Profession: 'Τι δουλειά κάνεις;' or 'Με τι ασχολείσαι;'
• Cardinal Numerals: μηδέν (0), ένας/μία/ένα (1), δέκα (10), είκοσι (20), εκατό (100).

entries.notes: Neuter in -μα with plural in -ματα. Core field on KEG exam personal registration forms.
entries.example_el: Ποιο είναι το επάγγελμά σας;
entries.example_en: What is your profession?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about and stating occupational status

entries.notes: Proparoxytone masculine in -ος (accent shifts in genitive, but stays stable at A1 nominative/accusative).
entries.example_el: Ο δάσκαλος διδάσκει τα παιδιά στην τάξη.
entries.example_en: The teacher teaches the children in the classroom.

entries.notes: Feminine equivalent of ο δάσκαλος; regular feminine in -α with plural in -ες.
entries.example_el: Η δασκάλα είναι πολύ ευγενική.
entries.example_en: The teacher is very kind.

entries.notes: Masculine in -ης (plural: -ες). Used for both high school teachers and university professors.
entries.example_el: Ο καθηγητής διδάσκει στο πανεπιστήμιο.
entries.example_en: The professor teaches at the university.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying secondary or tertiary academic instructors

entries.notes: Feminine suffix -τρια derived from masculine in -τής (ο καθηγητής -> η καθηγήτρια).
entries.example_el: Η κυρία Ανδρέου είναι καθηγήτρια γαλλικών.
entries.example_en: Mrs. Andreou is a French teacher.

entries.notes: Masculine noun in -ης. Note distinction: μαθητής (school pupil) vs φοιτητής (university student).
entries.example_el: Ο Νίκος είναι επιμελής μαθητής.
entries.example_en: Nikos is a diligent student.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying male primary or secondary school students

entries.notes: Feminine in -τρια (plural: οι μαθήτριες).
entries.example_el: Η Μαρία είναι μαθήτρια στο γυμνάσιο.
entries.example_en: Maria is a student in middle school.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying female primary or secondary school students

entries.notes: Refers strictly to tertiary/higher education students.
entries.example_el: Είμαι φοιτητής ιατρικής.
entries.example_en: I am a medical student.

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο φοιτητής.
entries.example_el: Η Άννα είναι φοιτήτρια στην Αθήνα.
entries.example_en: Anna is a university student in Athens.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine in -ός. In modern Greek, often used with feminine article for female doctors: η γιατρός.
entries.example_el: Ο γιατρός εξετάζει τον ασθενή.
entries.example_en: The doctor is examining the patient.

entries.notes: Compound from νόσος (illness) + κομώ (care for). Male form is ο νοσοκόμος.
entries.example_el: Η νοσοκόμα δουλεύει στο νοσοκομείο.
entries.example_en: The nurse works at the hospital.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing nursing staff and hospital personnel

entries.notes: Compound from δίκη (trial/justice) + αγορεύω (speak publicly). Female lawyer: η δικηγόρος.
entries.example_el: Ο δικηγόρος έχει γραφείο στο κέντρο.
entries.example_en: The lawyer has an office in the city centre.

entries.notes: Common-gender noun: ο γραμματέας (male), η γραμματέας (female). Plural: οι γραμματείς.
entries.example_el: Η γραμματέας απαντάει στο τηλέφωνο.
entries.example_en: The secretary answers the phone.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone noun in -ος. Female equivalent is η υπάλληλος.
entries.example_el: Είναι υπάλληλος σε μία τράπεζα.
entries.example_en: He/she is an employee in a bank.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing employment in offices, stores, and banks

entries.notes: Agent noun in -τής with oxytone stress.
entries.example_el: Ο πωλητής εξυπηρετεί τους πελάτες.
entries.example_en: The shop assistant serves the customers.

entries.notes: Feminine agent suffix -τρια with paroxytone stress (η πωλήτρια).
entries.example_el: Η πωλήτρια δουλεύει σε κατάστημα ρούχων.
entries.example_en: The saleswoman works in a clothing store.

entries.notes: From French 'serviteur'. Standard paroxytone masculine in -ος.
entries.example_el: Ο σερβιτόρος φέρνει τον κατάλογο.
entries.example_en: The waiter brings the menu.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Addressing and describing dining staff in tavernas and cafes

entries.notes: Feminine form of ο σερβιτόρος.
entries.example_el: Η σερβιτόρα παίρνει την παραγγελία.
entries.example_en: The waitress takes the order.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine in -ός (plural: οι οδηγοί). Used for drivers (ταξί, λεωφορείου) and tourist guides.
entries.example_el: Ο οδηγός του λεωφορείου είναι πολύ προσεκτικός.
entries.example_en: The bus driver is very careful.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone masculine in -ας with plural in -ες (οι μάγειρες).
entries.example_el: Ο μάγειρας ετοιμάζει νόστιμο φαγητό.
entries.example_en: The chef prepares delicious food.

entries.notes: Regular neuter in -ο. Governed by 'σε + άρθρο' (στο γραφείο).
entries.example_el: Δουλεύω σε ένα μεγάλο γραφείο.
entries.example_en: I work in a big office.

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -είο (plural: τα σχολεία).
entries.example_el: Τα παιδιά πάνε στο σχολείο κάθε πρωί.
entries.example_en: The children go to school every morning.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to places of primary and secondary education

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter in -ιο (plural: τα πανεπιστήμια).
entries.example_el: Σπουδάζω νομικά στο πανεπιστήμιο.
entries.example_en: I study law at the university.

entries.notes: Neuter in -είο. Frequent landmark in KEG city direction questions.
entries.example_el: Ο γιατρός είναι τώρα στο νοσοκομείο.
entries.example_en: The doctor is at the hospital right now.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to healthcare workplaces and facilities

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -εια (plural: οι εταιρείες).
entries.example_el: Δουλεύει σε μία πολυεθνική εταιρεία.
entries.example_en: He/she works at a multinational company.

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -ση with plural in -σεις. Core item in KEG Writing Task 1 forms.
entries.example_el: Ποια είναι η διεύθυνσή σας;
entries.example_en: What is your address?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for and writing postal/residential address

entries.notes: Grammatical exception: feminine gender despite ending in -ος (accusative: την οδό).
entries.example_el: Μένω στην οδό Σταδίου, στον αριθμό 10.
entries.example_en: I live on Stadiou Street, at number 10.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying street names on contact forms

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine noun in -ός (plural: οι αριθμοί).
entries.example_el: Ποιος είναι ο αριθμός του σπιτιού σου;
entries.example_en: What is your house number?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating house, flat, and phone numbers

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter. Takes enclitic accent before possessive pronoun: το τηλέφωνό μου.
entries.example_el: Ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνό σου;
entries.example_en: What is your phone number?

entries.notes: Short for 'το κινητό τηλέφωνο'. Always neuter in -ό.
entries.example_el: Έχεις το κινητό της Μαρίας;
entries.example_en: Do you have Maria's mobile number?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Giving and asking for mobile phone numbers

entries.notes: Compound from ταχύς (swift) + δρόμος (run/path). Abbreviated on Greek signs as ΕΛΤΑ.
entries.example_el: Το ταχυδρομείο είναι ανοιχτό μέχρι τις δύο.
entries.example_en: The post office is open until two o'clock.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to postal services and public buildings

entries.notes: Often abbreviated as Τ.Κ. in Greek forms and exam papers.
entries.example_el: Ο ταχυδρομικός κώδικας της περιοχής είναι 10679.
entries.example_en: The postal code of the area is 10679.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Completing postal code entries on registration forms

entries.english: to work / to have a job
entries.notes: Standard Type A active verb (-ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν). Synonym of εργάζομαι.
entries.example_el: Δουλεύω ως προγραμματιστής στην Αθήνα.
entries.example_en: I work as a developer in Athens.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about current work, employment, and workplace

entries.notes: Distinct from 'διαβάζω' (to read / do homework): 'σπουδάζω' means enrolled in higher education studies.
entries.example_el: Σπουδάζω αρχιτεκτονική στο πολυτεχνείο.
entries.example_en: I am studying architecture at the polytechnic.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about university majors and fields of study

entries.notes: Oxytone indeclinable numeral.
entries.example_el: Το τηλέφωνό μου αρχίζει από μηδέν.
entries.example_en: My phone number starts with zero.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Dictating and reading phone numbers and postal codes

entries.notes: The numbers 1, 3, 4 inflect for gender in Modern Greek. Masculine accusative is 'έναν' before vowels/plosives.
entries.example_el: Έχω έναν αδελφό και μία αδελφή.
entries.example_en: I have one brother and one sister.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Counting units and serving as the indefinite article

entries.notes: Indeclinable cardinal numeral.
entries.example_el: Μένω στον αριθμό δέκα.
entries.example_en: I live at number ten.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating quantities, street numbers, and dates

entries.notes: Indeclinable cardinal base for numbers 21-29 (είκοσι ένα, είκοσι δύο...).
entries.example_el: Είμαι είκοσι χρονών.
entries.example_en: I am twenty years old.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Telling age, prices, and contact details

entries.notes: Takes final -ν in compound numerals starting with a vowel: εκατόν ένα (101), εκατόν οκτώ (108).
entries.example_el: Το εισιτήριο κάνει εκατό ευρώ.
entries.example_en: The ticket costs one hundred euros.

grammatical_info.euphonic_variant: εκατόν (before vowels in compounds, e.g. εκατόν ένα)

entries.keg_communicative_function: Reading three-digit numbers, prices, and street addresses

entries.notes: Must always be written with a written accent (τόνος) in questions to distinguish from the relative pronoun 'που'.
entries.example_el: Πού δουλεύετε;
entries.example_en: Where do you work?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for workplace, residence, and geographical location

lessons.title: Οικογένεια, Πρόσωπα & Περιγραφή (Family & Physical/Personal Traits)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Family relations, marital status, physical descriptions, the verb 'έχω', and possessive enclitics (μου, σου, του, της).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 4 Core Grammar Notes:
• Verb 'έχω' (Present Active): εγώ έχω, εσύ έχεις, αυτός/αυτή/αυτό έχει, εμείς έχουμε, εσείς έχετε, αυτοί/αυτές/αυτά έχουν.
• Weak Possessive Clitics: Placed directly after the noun (ο πατέρας μου, η μητέρα σου, το παιδί μας).
• Definite Article Rule: Possessive clitics always require the definite article before the noun: 'το μωρό μου' (NOT 'μωρό μου' in declarative statements).
• Adjective Agreement: Masculine in -ος, Feminine in -η/-α, Neuter in -ο (ψηλός, ψηλή, ψηλό; νέος, νέα, νέο).

entries.notes: Feminine in -εια (plural: οι οικογένειες). Theme word for KEG personal description emails.
entries.example_el: Έχω μία μεγάλη οικογένεια.
entries.example_en: I have a big family.

entries.notes: Plural noun in -είς. Accusative plural is 'τους γονείς'.
entries.example_el: Οι γονείς μου μένουν στη Θεσσαλονίκη.
entries.example_en: My parents live in Thessaloniki.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about father and mother collectively

entries.notes: Paroxytone masculine in -ας (plural: οι πατέρες). Accusative drops final -ς: τον πατέρα.
entries.example_el: Ο πατέρας μου είναι γιατρός.
entries.example_en: My father is a doctor.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying one's father in family descriptions

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α (plural: οι μητέρες).
entries.example_el: Η μητέρα μου είναι δασκάλα.
entries.example_en: My mother is a teacher.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Identifying one's mother in family descriptions

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine in -άς; forms plural with suffix -άδες (οι μπαμπάδες).
entries.example_el: Ο μπαμπάς μου μαγειρεύει πολύ καλά.
entries.example_en: My dad cooks very well.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Informal and affectionate reference to father

entries.notes: Oxytone feminine in -ά; plural takes suffix -άδες (οι μαμάδες).
entries.example_el: Η μαμά μου είναι πολύ γλυκιά.
entries.example_en: My mom is very sweet.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Informal and affectionate reference to mother

entries.notes: Monosyllabic masculine with diphthong (ο γιος, οι γιοι, τους γιους).
entries.example_el: Έχουν έναν γιο και μία κόρη.
entries.example_en: They have a son and a daughter.

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -η with plural in -ες (οι κόρες).
entries.example_el: Η κόρη τους σπουδάζει στην Αγγλία.
entries.example_en: Their daughter is studying in England.

entries.notes: Both forms 'αδελφός' (formal/written) and 'αδερφός' (spoken/demotic) are standard in Greece.
entries.example_el: Ο αδελφός μου είναι είκοσι πέντε χρονών.
entries.example_en: My brother is twenty-five years old.

entries.notes: Oxytone feminine in -ή (plural in -ές).
entries.example_el: Η αδελφή μου δουλεύει σε τράπεζα.
entries.example_en: My sister works at a bank.

entries.notes: Spelled with double π (ππ). Plural forms in -ούδες: οι παππούδες.
entries.example_el: Ο παππούς μου είναι εβδομήντα χρονών.
entries.example_en: My grandfather is seventy years old.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about grandparents and elderly family members

entries.notes: Oxytone feminine with plural in -άδες (οι γιαγιάδες).
entries.example_el: Η γιαγιά μου φτιάχνει τέλεια πίτα.
entries.example_en: My grandmother makes perfect pie.

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ί (plural: τα παιδιά). Colloquially used among young adults: 'Γεια σας, παιδιά!' (Hi guys!).
entries.example_el: Έχουν δύο παιδιά.
entries.example_en: They have two children.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to children or family dependents

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ό with plural in -ά (τα μωρά).
entries.example_el: Το μωρό κοιμάται τώρα.
entries.example_en: The baby is sleeping right now.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to infants and very young children

entries.notes: Paroxytone masculine in -ας. Context determines whether it means 'man' or 'husband'.
entries.example_el: Ο άντρας της είναι αρχιτέκτονας.
entries.example_en: Her husband is an architect.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to an adult male or one's husband

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α. Context determines whether it means 'woman' or 'wife'.
entries.example_el: Η γυναίκα μου δουλεύει στο πανεπιστήμιο.
entries.example_en: My wife works at the university.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to an adult female or one's wife

entries.notes: Regular masculine in -ος (plural: οι θείοι).
entries.example_el: Ο θείος μου μένει στην Κρήτη.
entries.example_en: My uncle lives in Crete.

entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of ο θείος.
entries.example_el: Η θεία Ελένη έχει τρία παιδιά.
entries.example_en: Aunt Eleni has three children.

entries.notes: Both forms 'ξάδελφος' and 'ξάδερφος' are standard. Takes second accent with clitic: ο ξάδελφός μου.
entries.example_el: Ο ξάδελφός μου σπουδάζει πληροφορική.
entries.example_en: My cousin is studying computer science.

entries.notes: Feminine form in -η (plural: οι ξαδέλφες).
entries.example_el: Η ξαδέλφη μου μένει δίπλα στο σπίτι μας.
entries.example_en: My cousin lives next to our house.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone masculine in -ος (root of English 'anthropology').
entries.example_el: Είναι πολύ καλός άνθρωπος.
entries.example_en: He is a very good person.

entries.notes: Participle used as descriptive adjective of marital status (οικογενειακή κατάσταση).
entries.example_el: Είστε παντρεμένος ή ελεύθερος;
entries.example_en: Are you married or single?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating marital status on questionnaires and forms

entries.notes: Standard demographic term for 'single / unmarried' on Greek registration forms.
entries.example_el: Ο αδελφός μου είναι ακόμη ελεύθερος.
entries.example_en: My brother is still single.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter in -ο. Takes second accent with possessive: το πρόσωπό του.
entries.example_el: Έχει πολύ γλυκό πρόσωπο.
entries.example_en: He/she has a very sweet face.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing facial features and physical appearance

entries.notes: Modern Greek expresses head hair in the plural neuter (τα μαλλιά).
entries.example_el: Η Ελένη έχει μακριά καστανά μαλλιά.
entries.example_en: Eleni has long brown hair.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing hair color and style in physical descriptions

entries.notes: Neuter plural of 'το μάτι'. Common colors: μπλε (blue), πράσινα (green), καστανά (brown).
entries.example_el: Ο γιος μου έχει μπλε μάτια.
entries.example_en: My son has blue eyes.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing eye color in person descriptions

entries.notes: Oxytone adjective. Spelled with ψι (ψ) + ήτα (η).
entries.example_el: Ο πατέρας μου είναι ψηλός άντρας.
entries.example_en: My father is a tall man.

entries.notes: Direct antonym of ψηλός.
entries.example_el: Η αδελφή μου είναι λίγο κοντή.
entries.example_en: My sister is a little short.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone adjective in -ος, -η, -ο. Alpha-privative: α- + δυνατός (not strong / thin).
entries.example_el: Ο Νίκος είναι ψηλός και αδύνατος.
entries.example_en: Nikos is tall and slim.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing slender build or body type

entries.notes: Oxytone regular adjective.
entries.example_el: Φοράει ένα χοντρό παλτό.
entries.example_en: He/she is wearing a thick coat.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing body build or thick objects

entries.notes: Proparoxytone adjective (accent on first syllable ό-).
entries.example_el: Η μητέρα της είναι πολύ όμορφη γυναίκα.
entries.example_en: Her mother is a very beautiful woman.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing attractive appearance of persons or places

entries.notes: Feminine ends in -α (νέα) because a vowel precedes the ending.
entries.example_el: Ο καθηγητής μας είναι αρκετά νέος.
entries.example_en: Our professor is quite young.

entries.notes: When referring to people, 'μεγάλος' is the polite way to say older/elderly (rather than γέρος).
entries.example_el: Ο παππούς μου είναι μεγάλος άνθρωπος.
entries.example_en: My grandfather is an elderly person.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Describing older age or large size

entries.notes: Base oxytone adjective used in numerous daily formulas (καλημέρα, καλό ταξίδι).
entries.example_el: Είναι πολύ καλοί φίλοι.
entries.example_en: They are very good friends.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing positive character and quality evaluation

entries.notes: False friend: means 'likeable/pleasant', not 'feeling pity/sympathy'.
entries.example_el: Η νέα γειτόνισσα είναι πολύ συμπαθητική.
entries.example_en: The new neighbor is very likeable.

entries.notes: Crucial verb for A1 personal descriptions. Present: έχω, έχεις, έχει, έχουμε, έχετε, έχουν.
entries.example_el: Έχω δύο αδέλφια και έναν σκύλο.
entries.example_en: I have two siblings and a dog.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing family relations, age, and possession

entries.notes: Enclitic follows the noun. Causes a second accent if noun is proparoxytone: το αυτοκίνητό μου.
entries.example_el: Αυτή είναι η μητέρα μου.
entries.example_en: This is my mother.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Indicating family relations and personal ownership

entries.notes: Informal singular possessive clitic.
entries.example_el: Πώς λένε τον αδελφό σου;
entries.example_en: What is your brother's name?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about someone's family or possessions

entries.notes: Agrees with the possessor, not the possessed object: το σπίτι της (her house), το σπίτι του (his house).
entries.example_el: Ο άντρας της είναι καθηγητής.
entries.example_en: Her husband is a professor.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing possession relating to a third person

entries.notes: 'σας' is used politely to a single person: 'Ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνό σας;'.
entries.example_el: Αυτός είναι ο καθηγητής μας.
entries.example_en: This is our professor.

grammatical_info.forms: μας (1st pl), σας (2nd pl/polite), τους (3rd pl)

entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing group possession and polite address

units.title: Στο Καφέ & Στην Ταβέρνα (Ordering Food & Drinks)

lessons.title: Στο Καφέ & Στην Ταβέρνα (Ordering Food & Drinks)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Reading Greek menus, ordering food and drinks, coffee preparation styles, taverna etiquette, and consumption verbs (θέλω, πίνω, παίρνω, τρώω).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 5 Core Grammar Notes:

• Verbs of Consumption & Preference (Present Active Indicative):
  - θέλω (Type A): θέλω, θέλεις, θέλει, θέλουμε, θέλετε, θέλουν.
  - πίνω (Type A): πίνω, πίνεις, πίνει, πίνουμε, πίνετε, πίνουν.
  - παίρνω (Type A): παίρνω, παίρνεις, παίρνει, παίρνουμε, παίρνετε, παίρνουν.
  - τρώω (Type A irregular): τρώω, τρως, τρώει, τρώμε, τρώτε, τρώνε.

• Direct Object in Accusative with Indefinite Article:
  - Masculine: έναν καφέ, έναν χυμό
  - Feminine: μία μπίρα (μπύρα), μία σαλάτα
  - Neuter: ένα νερό, ένα τοστ, ένα σουβλάκι

• Greek Coffee Sweetness Degrees:
  - σκέτος (plain / zero sugar)
  - μέτριος (medium / 1 spoon sugar)
  - γλυκός (sweet / 2 spoons sugar)

• Common Ordering Formulas:
  - 'Τι θα πάρετε;' (What will you have?)
  - 'Για μένα... παρακαλώ.' (For me... please.)
  - 'Τον λογαριασμό, παρακαλώ.' (The bill, please.)
  - 'Ορίστε!' (Here you are! / Certainly!)
  - 'Καλή όρεξη!' (Enjoy your meal!) / 'Στην υγειά μας!' (Cheers!)

entries.notes: Masculine in -ές. Plural adds -έδες (οι καφέδες). Direct object accusative: έναν καφέ.
entries.example_el: Έναν ελληνικό καφέ μέτριο, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A medium-sweet Greek coffee, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering beverages at a cafe or traditional kafeneio

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ό. Served automatically in carafes or bottles in Greek cafes.
entries.example_el: Ένα μπουκάλι νερό, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A bottle of water, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for water in dining establishments

entries.notes: Neuter in -ι with diphthong (plural: τα τσάγια). 'Τσάι του βουνού' (mountain tea) is an iconic Greek herbal tea.
entries.example_el: Πίνω ζεστό τσάι του βουνού με μέλι.
entries.example_en: I drink hot mountain tea with honey.

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine in -ός (accusative: τον χυμό). Note: 'φρέσκος χυμός' = fresh-squeezed juice.
entries.example_el: Θέλω έναν φρέσκο χυμό πορτοκάλι.
entries.example_en: I want a fresh orange juice.

entries.notes: In Greece, waiters will ask: 'Με ανθρακικό ή χωρίς;' (Sparkling or still?).
entries.example_el: Μία πορτοκαλάδα με ανθρακικό, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: An orangeade with carbonation, please.

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α with plural in -ες.
entries.example_el: Για μένα μία κρύα λεμονάδα.
entries.example_en: For me a cold lemonade.

entries.notes: Irregular neuter noun: adds -τ- in plural (τα γάλατα). 'Με γάλα' = with milk, 'χωρίς γάλα' = without milk.
entries.example_el: Θέλετε τον καφέ με γάλα ή χωρίς γάλα;
entries.example_en: Do you want the coffee with milk or without milk?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying coffee additives or ordering breakfast beverages

entries.notes: Both spellings 'μπίρα' (simplified official) and 'μπύρα' (traditional) are prevalent across Greece.
entries.example_el: Φέρτε μας δύο κρύες μπίρες, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: Bring us two cold beers, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering alcoholic beverages in tavernas and bars

entries.notes: In Greek tavernas, house wine is ordered by the kilo/half-kilo (μισό κιλό χύμα κρασί).
entries.example_el: Παίρνουμε μισό κιλό κόκκινο κρασί.
entries.example_en: We take half a kilo of red wine.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone feminine in -η (plural: οι ζάχαρες). Preposition 'χωρίς' takes accusative: χωρίς ζάχαρη.
entries.example_el: Πίνω τον καφέ μου χωρίς ζάχαρη.
entries.example_en: I drink my coffee without sugar.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying sweetness level for hot and iced beverages

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ό. Derived from ancient verb φαγεῖν (to eat).
entries.example_el: Το ελληνικό φαγητό είναι πολύ νόστιμο.
entries.example_en: Greek food is very tasty.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about cuisine and meals in general

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ί (plural: τα ψωμιά). Staple accompanied item in every Greek meal.
entries.example_el: Μας φέρνετε λίγο ψωμί, παρακαλώ;
entries.example_en: Could you bring us some bread, please?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Requesting bread basket at the table

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α with plural in -ες (οι σαλάτες).
entries.example_el: Θέλουμε μία πράσινη σαλάτα.
entries.example_en: We want a green salad.

entries.notes: Literally: 'village salad'. In Greece, salads are traditionally placed 'για τη μέση' (to share).
entries.example_el: Παίρνουμε μία χωριάτικη σαλάτα για τη μέση.
entries.example_en: We take a Greek salad to share (for the middle of the table).

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ί (plural: τα τυριά).
entries.example_el: Μου αρέσει πολύ το ελληνικό τυρί.
entries.example_en: I like Greek cheese very much.

entries.notes: Also means 'slice' (e.g. μία φέτα ψωμί = a slice of bread).
entries.example_el: Θέλουμε ψητή φέτα με μέλι και σουσάμι.
entries.example_en: We want baked feta with honey and sesame.

entries.notes: Neuter in -ας with plural in -ατα (τα κρέατα).
entries.example_el: Δεν τρώω κρέας, είμαι χορτοφάγος.
entries.example_en: I do not eat meat, I am a vegetarian.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about main courses or dietary preferences

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter in -ο (plural: τα κοτόπουλα).
entries.example_el: Για κυρίως πιάτο θέλω κοτόπουλο με πατάτες.
entries.example_en: For main dish I want chicken with potatoes.

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ι (plural: τα ψάρια).
entries.example_el: Έχετε φρέσκο ψάρι σήμερα;
entries.example_en: Do you have fresh fish today?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering seafood and fresh fish at seaside tavernas

entries.notes: Diminutive of σούβλα (spit). Plural: τα σουβλάκια.
entries.example_el: Παίρνουμε δύο σουβλάκια με πίτα και τζατζίκι.
entries.example_en: We take two souvlakia with pita and tzatziki.

entries.notes: Refers both to flatbread for souvlaki and filo pastry pies (τυρόπιτα).
entries.example_el: Θέλω ένα σουβλάκι σε πίτα.
entries.example_en: I want a souvlaki in pita bread.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering pita wraps or bakery pies (τυρόπιτα, σπανακόπιτα)

entries.notes: In taverna menus, 'πατάτες τηγανητές' (fried potatoes / fries) is universally ordered in the plural.
entries.example_el: Μία μερίδα πατάτες τηγανητές, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: One portion of french fries, please.

entries.notes: Foreign loanword: indeclinable neuter noun (το τοστ / τα τοστ).
entries.example_el: Ένα τοστ με γαλοπούλα και τυρί.
entries.example_en: A toasted sandwich with turkey and cheese.

entries.notes: Substantivized neuter adjective: το γλυκό (the sweet/dessert), plural: τα γλυκά.
entries.example_el: Τι γλυκό έχετε σήμερα;
entries.example_en: What dessert do you have today?

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ό (plural: τα παγωτά). Root: παγώνω (to freeze).
entries.example_el: Θέλω ένα παγωτό σοκολάτα.
entries.example_en: I want a chocolate ice cream.

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -είο. Iconic pillar of Greek community life.
entries.example_el: Οι ηλικιωμένοι πίνουν καφέ στο παραδοσιακό καφενείο.
entries.example_en: The elderly drink coffee at the traditional coffeehouse.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to historic Greek social meeting venues

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -ια (plural: οι καφετέριες). Refers to modern cafes (serving freddo espresso/cappuccino).
entries.example_el: Συναντιόμαστε στην καφετέρια στην πλατεία.
entries.example_en: We meet at the cafe in the square.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Arranging social meetings at contemporary cafes

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α. Core cultural keyword in KEG exam listening dialogues.
entries.example_el: Το βράδυ τρώμε σε μία ψαροταβέρνα.
entries.example_en: In the evening we eat at a seafood taverna.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Choosing dining venues for lunch or dinner

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter in -ιο (plural: τα εστιατόρια).
entries.example_el: Αυτό το εστιατόριο έχει εξαιρετική θέα.
entries.example_en: This restaurant has an excellent view.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to restaurants and dining establishments

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ι. Phrase 'κάνω το τραπέζι' = to treat someone to a meal.
entries.example_el: Ένα τραπέζι για τέσσερα άτομα, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A table for four people, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Requesting seating in restaurants and cafes

entries.notes: Proparoxytone masculine in -ος (plural: οι κατάλογοι). In tavernas also called 'το μενού'.
entries.example_el: Μας φέρνετε τον κατάλογο, παρακαλώ;
entries.example_en: Could you bring us the menu, please?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for the food or drink menu

entries.notes: Oxytone masculine in -ός (accusative: τον λογαριασμό). Universal payment formula in Greece.
entries.example_el: Τον λογαριασμό, παρακαλώ!
entries.example_en: The bill, please!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for the check at the end of a meal

entries.notes: Compound from φίλος (friend) + δώρο (gift). Proparoxytone neuter in -μα.
entries.example_el: Αφήνουμε φιλοδώρημα στο τραπέζι.
entries.example_en: We leave a tip on the table.

entries.notes: Core Type A modal verb. Present: θέλω, θέλεις, θέλει, θέλουμε, θέλετε, θέλουν. Triggers 'να + verb': θέλω να παραγγείλω.
entries.example_el: Θέλω ένα ποτήρι κρύο νερό.
entries.example_en: I want a glass of cold water.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Expressing wishes and placing dining orders

entries.notes: Type A active verb. Present paradigm: πίνω, πίνεις, πίνει, πίνουμε, πίνετε, πίνουν.
entries.example_el: Τι πίνετε; — Πίνω έναν ζεστό καφέ.
entries.example_en: What are you drinking? — I am drinking a hot coffee.

entries.english: to take / to order / to have (food/drink)
entries.notes: Type A active verb. In ordering context, 'παίρνω' is the most natural verb: 'Τι θα πάρετε;' (What will you have?).
entries.example_el: Εγώ παίρνω μία χωριάτικη σαλάτα και ένα σουβλάκι.
entries.example_en: I will take a Greek salad and a souvlaki.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Standard conversational verb used when placing orders

entries.notes: Contracted present forms: τρώω, τρως, τρώει, τρώμε, τρώτε, τρώνε. Note spelling with omega and tonos.
entries.example_el: Τρώμε μεσημεριανό στις δύο.
entries.example_en: We eat lunch at two o'clock.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about food consumption and dietary habits

entries.notes: Type A active verb: παραγγέλνω, παραγγέλνεις, παραγγέλνει, παραγγέλνουμε, παραγγέλνετε, παραγγέλνουν.
entries.example_el: Είμαστε έτοιμοι να παραγγείλουμε.
entries.example_en: We are ready to order.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Explicitly initiating an order at a restaurant or shop

entries.english: here you are / certainly / what can I get you?
entries.notes: Versatile Greek particle: used when handing over items ('Here you go'), answering the door/phone ('Yes?'), or acknowledging a customer.
entries.example_el: — Έναν καφέ, παρακαλώ. — Ορίστε, ο καφές σας!
entries.example_en: — A coffee, please. — Here you are, your coffee!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Handing something over or responding politely to customers

entries.notes: Preposition 'για' takes strong accusative: για μένα (for me), για σένα (for you).
entries.example_el: Για μένα μία μπίρα, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: For me a beer, please.

grammatical_info.structure: για + strong personal pronoun in accusative (μένα)

entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying one's individual choice in a group order

entries.english: what will you have? / what can I get you?
entries.notes: The universal question posed by Greek waiters and kiosk clerks to start a transaction.
entries.example_el: Γεια σας, τι θα πάρετε παρακαλώ;
entries.example_en: Hello, what will you have, please?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Understanding standard waiter inquiry in listening tests

entries.notes: Literally: 'Good appetite'. Addressed to anyone sitting down to eat.
entries.example_el: Το φαγητό έφτασε. Καλή όρεξη σε όλους!
entries.example_en: The food has arrived. Enjoy your meal, everyone!
entries.keg_communicative_function: Wishing dining companions a pleasant meal

entries.notes: Contraction of 'σε + την υγεία μας'. Also commonly shortened to 'γεια μας!'.
entries.example_el: Στην υγειά μας, παιδιά!
entries.example_en: Cheers, guys! (To our health!)
entries.keg_communicative_function: Making toasts when drinking wine or beer

entries.notes: In Greek coffee culture: 'μέτριος' means 1 spoon of coffee and 1 spoon of sugar.
entries.example_el: Έναν φραπέ μέτριο με γάλα, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A medium-sweet frappé with milk, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying sweetness level when ordering Greek coffee or frappé

entries.notes: The three standard coffee sugar levels are: σκέτος (0 sugar), μέτριος (1 sugar), γλυκός (2 sugar).
entries.example_el: Πίνω τον καφέ πάντα σκέτο.
entries.example_en: I always drink my coffee plain (without sugar).
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering unsweetened coffee or plain food items

units.title: Στην Αγορά, Ψώνια & Τιμές (Shopping, Supermarket & Prices)

lessons.title: Στην Αγορά, Ψώνια & Τιμές (Shopping, Supermarket & Prices)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Supermarket shopping, farmers' market transactions, buying groceries and clothes, asking for prices and weights, and payment methods.
lessons.lesson_notes:
Unit 6 Core Grammar Notes:

• Inquiring about Prices:
  - Singular: 'Πόσο κάνει;' / 'Πόσο κοστίζει;' (e.g. Πόσο κάνει το γάλα;)
  - Plural: 'Πόσο έχουν;' / 'Πόσο κάνουν;' (e.g. Πόσο έχουν τα πορτοκάλια;)

• Units of Measurement & Packaging:
  - το κιλό (kilo) / μισό κιλό (half kilo)
  - το γραμμάριο (gram) / διακόσια γραμμάρια (200g)
  - το λίτρο (liter) / το μπουκάλι (bottle) / το πακέτο (packet)

• Neuter Nouns in -ο, -ι, -μα:
  - In -ο: το κιλό -> τα κιλά, το λίτρο -> τα λίτρα, το μήλο -> τα μήλα.
  - In -ι: το ψωμί -> τα ψωμιά, το τυρί -> τα τυριά, το μαγαζί -> τα μαγαζιά.
  - In -μα: το χρώμα -> τα χρώματα, το πράγμα -> τα πράγματα.

• Payment Methods:
  - με μετρητά (with cash)
  - με κάρτα (by card)

• Key Commercial Expressions:
  - 'Ορίστε τα ρέστα σας.' (Here is your change.)
  - 'Χρειάζεστε απόδειξη;' (Do you need a receipt?)
  - 'Ψάχνω ένα...' (I am looking for a...)

entries.notes: Feminine in -ά with plural in -ές. Also means the abstract economy or financial market.
entries.example_el: Πάω στην κεντρική αγορά για ψώνια.
entries.example_en: I am going to the central market for shopping.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about and identifying shopping venues

entries.notes: Universally referred to as 'η λαϊκή'. Core cultural setting in KEG listening exams.
entries.example_el: Κάθε Σάββατο πηγαίνουμε στη λαϊκή.
entries.example_en: Every Saturday we go to the street market.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Shopping for fresh agricultural produce in Greece

entries.notes: Indeclinable neuter loanword.
entries.example_el: Κάνω τα ψώνια της εβδομάδας στο σούπερ μάρκετ.
entries.example_en: I do the week's shopping at the supermarket.

entries.notes: Masculine in -ος (plural: οι φούρνοι). Synonym of 'το αρτοποιείο'.
entries.example_el: Αγοράζω φρέσκο ψωμί από τον φούρνο.
entries.example_en: I buy fresh bread from the bakery.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Buying bread, bakery goods, and morning pies

entries.notes: Compound of κρέας (meat) + πωλώ (to sell). Paroxytone neuter in -είο.
entries.example_el: Το κρεοπωλείο είναι δίπλα στον φούρνο.
entries.example_en: The butcher shop is next to the bakery.

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ί (plural: τα μαγαζιά). Synonym of 'το κατάστημα'.
entries.example_el: Τα μαγαζιά κλείνουν στις εννέα το βράδυ.
entries.example_en: The shops close at nine in the evening.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Referring to commercial stores in general

entries.notes: Neuter in -ι (plural: τα λάδια). 'Ελαιόλαδο' specifically denotes olive oil.
entries.example_el: Χρειαζόμαστε ένα λίτρο ελαιόλαδο.
entries.example_en: We need one liter of olive oil.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Purchasing cooking oil and Greek staple products

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ι.
entries.example_el: Ένα πακέτο ρύζι για πιλάφι, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A package of rice for pilaf, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Buying grain staples at the supermarket

entries.notes: Plural noun in Greek (τα μακαρόνια). Spelled with one κ.
entries.example_el: Αγοράζω δύο πακέτα μακαρόνια.
entries.example_en: I am buying two packets of pasta.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Buying pasta on grocery shopping trips

entries.notes: Neuter plural (singular: το φρούτο).
entries.example_el: Στη λαϊκή έχει πάντα φρέσκα φρούτα.
entries.example_en: At the street market there is always fresh fruit.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Shopping at greengrocers or open markets

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter plural (singular: το λαχανικό).
entries.example_el: Τρώμε πολλά λαχανικά για υγεία.
entries.example_en: We eat a lot of vegetables for good health.

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α with plural in -ες. Accusative keeps -ν before ντ: 'την ντομάτα'.
entries.example_el: Βάλτε μου δύο κιλά ντομάτες για σαλάτα.
entries.example_en: Give me two kilos of tomatoes for salad.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying produce quantities at the market

entries.notes: Spelled with double γ (γγ pronounced [ŋg]). Neuter in -ι.
entries.example_el: Θέλω μισό κιλό αγγούρια.
entries.example_en: I want half a kilo of cucumbers.

entries.notes: Spelled with double μ (μμ) and upsilon (υ).
entries.example_el: Ένα κιλό ξερά κρεμμύδια, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: One kilo of dry onions, please.

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ο with plural in -α (τα μήλα).
entries.example_el: Πόσο έχουν τα κόκκινα μήλα;
entries.example_en: How much are the red apples?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about fruit prices and buying fruit

entries.notes: Distinguish: 'πορτοκάλι' (noun fruit) vs 'πορτοκαλί' (indeclinable orange color).
entries.example_el: Δύο κιλά πορτοκάλια για χυμό, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: Two kilos of oranges for juicing, please.

entries.notes: Oxytone neuter in -ό (plural: τα κιλά). 'Μισό κιλό' = half a kilo.
entries.example_el: Ένα κιλό φέτα και μισό κιλό ελιές.
entries.example_en: One kilo of feta and half a kilo of olives.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Stating weights when buying food in Greece

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter. In Greek deli counters, portions are ordered in hundreds of grams (διακόσια γραμμάρια).
entries.example_el: Διακόσια γραμμάρια τυρί γκούντα σε φέτες.
entries.example_en: Two hundred grams of gouda cheese in slices.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Ordering sliced deli meats and cheese by weight

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ο.
entries.example_el: Ένα λίτρο φρέσκο γάλα.
entries.example_en: One liter of fresh milk.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying liquid volumes for milk, oil, or wine

entries.notes: Paroxytone neuter in -ι.
entries.example_el: Δύο μπουκάλια εμφιαλωμένο νερό.
entries.example_en: Two bottles of bottled water.

entries.notes: Also used in food take-out: 'σε πακέτο' / 'για πακέτο' (to go / take away).
entries.example_el: Ένα πακέτο μπισκότα για τα παιδιά.
entries.example_en: A packet of biscuits for the children.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Buying boxed or packaged goods (pasta, coffee, cookies)

entries.notes: Spelled with double μ (μμ). Plural: τα κομμάτια.
entries.example_el: Ένα κομμάτι τυρόπιτα, παρακαλώ.
entries.example_en: A piece of cheese pie, please.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for individual portions or pieces

entries.notes: Regular neuter in -ο. Almost always used in plural 'τα ρούχα' (clothes).
entries.example_el: Ψωνίζουμε ρούχα στις εκπτώσεις.
entries.example_en: We shop for clothes during the sales.

entries.notes: Grammatically singular in Greek (το παντελόνι) unlike English plural 'pants/trousers'.
entries.example_el: Δοκιμάζω ένα μαύρο παντελόνι.
entries.example_en: I am trying on a pair of black trousers.

entries.notes: Paroxytone feminine in -α with plural in -ες.
entries.example_el: Μου αρέσει αυτή η μπλε μπλούζα.
entries.example_en: I like this blue top.

entries.notes: Proparoxytone neuter in -ο (plural: τα πουκάμισα).
entries.example_el: Ψάχνω ένα άσπρο πουκάμισο για τη δουλειά.
entries.example_en: I am looking for a white shirt for work.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Shopping for formal or business attire

entries.notes: Neuter plural (singular: το παπούτσι).
entries.example_el: Αυτά τα παπούτσια είναι πολύ άνετα.
entries.example_en: These shoes are very comfortable.

entries.notes: Ancient declension neuter in -ος with plural in -η (τα μεγέθη). Note: shoe size is also called 'το νούμερο'.
entries.example_el: Τι μέγεθος φοράτε; — Φοράω medium.
entries.example_en: What size do you wear? — I wear medium.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for clothes size or shoe size

entries.notes: Neuter in -μα with plural in -ματα (τα χρώματα).
entries.example_el: Έχετε αυτό το φόρεμα σε άλλο χρώμα;
entries.example_en: Do you have this dress in another color?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for products in specific colors

entries.notes: Oxytone feminine in -ή. In receipts: 'Τιμή μονάδας' = unit price.
entries.example_el: Η τιμή είναι πολύ καλή για τέτοια ποιότητα.
entries.example_en: The price is very good for such quality.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Reading price tags or asking about costs

entries.notes: Plural only in commerce: τα ρέστα.
entries.example_el: Ορίστε τα ρέστα σας: πέντε ευρώ.
entries.example_en: Here is your change: five euros.

entries.notes: Feminine noun in -ση with plural in -σεις. Essential keyword in KEG reading tasks matching receipts to shopping lists.
entries.example_el: Μου δίνετε την απόδειξη, παρακαλώ;
entries.example_en: Could you give me the receipt, please?

entries.notes: From μετρώ (to count). Always plural: 'πληρώνω με μετρητά'.
entries.example_el: Πληρώνετε με μετρητά ή με κάρτα;
entries.example_en: Are you paying with cash or with card?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Specifying cash payment method at checkout

entries.notes: Universal payment method formula: 'με κάρτα'.
entries.example_el: Μπορώ να πληρώσω με κάρτα;
entries.example_en: Can I pay by card?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Paying by debit or credit card

entries.english: to buy / to purchase / I buy
entries.notes: Regular Type A active verb (-ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν). Derived from 'η αγορά'.
entries.example_el: Αγοράζω φρούτα από τη λαϊκή αγορά.
entries.example_en: I buy fruit from the street market.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Talking about purchasing goods and everyday items

entries.notes: Type A verb. Almost always used in 3rd person singular (κοστίζει) or 3rd person plural (κοστίζουν).
entries.example_el: Πόσο κοστίζει αυτό το παντελόνι;
entries.example_en: How much does this pair of trousers cost?
entries.keg_communicative_function: Inquiring about prices and costs of items

entries.notes: Type A active verb: πληρώνω, πληρώνεις, πληρώνει, πληρώνουμε, πληρώνετε, πληρώνουν.
entries.example_el: Πληρώνω στο ταμείο με κάρτα.
entries.example_en: I pay at the cash desk by card.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Executing payment transactions at stores and supermarkets

entries.english: to look for / to search for / I look for
entries.notes: Type A active verb. Directly takes direct object in accusative: ψάχνω το ταμείο.
entries.example_el: Καλημέρα σας, ψάχνω ένα ζεστό μπουφάν.
entries.example_en: Good morning, I am looking for a warm jacket.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking shop staff for assistance when locating items

entries.english: how much is it? / how much are they?
entries.notes: Singular agreement: 'Πόσο κάνει το τυρί;' / Plural agreement: 'Πόσο έχουν / κάνουν τα μήλα;'.
entries.example_el: — Πόσο κάνουν αυτά τα πορτοκάλια; — Ένα ευρώ το κιλό.
entries.example_en: — How much are these oranges? — One euro a kilo.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Asking for prices of singular and plural merchandise

entries.notes: Oxytone regular adjective. Direct antonym of 'φθηνός / φτηνός' (cheap / inexpensive).
entries.example_el: Αυτό το παλτό είναι πολύ ακριβό.
entries.example_en: This coat is very expensive.
entries.keg_communicative_function: Evaluating merchandise prices and comparing store costs

units.title: Κλικ στα Ελληνικά Α1: Σελίδες 25-41 (Εισαγωγική Ενότητα - Ήχοι, Γράμματα & Πρώτες Λέξεις)

lessons.title: Εισαγωγική Ενότητα: Ήχοι, Αλφάβητο & Βασικό Λεξιλόγιο (Pages 25-41)
lessons.description: CEFR A1: Phonetic patterns, alphabet letter combinations, and foundational vocabulary from Klik A1 (pages 25-41).
lessons.lesson_notes:
Κλικ στα Ελληνικά Α1 — Εισαγωγική Ενότητα (Σελίδες 25-41):
• Φωνηεντικά δίψηφα (Vowel Digraphs):
  - ει, οι, υι, η, ι, υ → [i]
  - αι, ε → [e]
  - ου → [u]
• Συνδυασμοί αυ, ευ (Combinations with υ):
  - Pronounced [af], [ef] before voiceless consonants (θ, κ, ξ, π, σ, τ, φ, χ, ψ).
  - Pronounced [av], [ev] before vowels and voiced consonants (β, γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν, ρ).
• Σύμφωνα & συμφωνικά δίψηφα (Consonants & Consonant Digraphs):
  - μπ → [b] at the start of a word, [mb]/[b] internally.
  - ντ → [d] at the start of a word, [nd]/[d] internally.
  - γκ / γγ → [g] at the start of a word, [ŋg]/[g] internally.
  - τσ → [ts], τζ → [dz].
• Διακριτικά σημεία (Diacritics):
  - Διαλυτικά (dialytika ¨): Separate vowels in digraphs (π.χ. το προϊόν, το καΐκι).
